articles.title: Chevron Announces JV Plans to Invest $7B in Venezuela
articles.description: Chevron Corporation announced that its joint ventures in Venezuela plan to invest more than $7 billion over the next five years.

articles.title: Diversified to Acquire Elliott Assets in Permian for $1.8B
articles.description: Diversified signed agreements to acquire Birch Permian from affiliates of Elliott for around $1.8 billion, supported by an expanded investment partnership with Carlyle.

articles.title: Ansaldo Energia advances fuel flexibility strategy to H₂ and HVO
articles.description: Ansaldo Energia has secured TÜV SÜD Hydrogen Readiness certification for its GT36 and DNV validation for HVO operation of the AE94.3A combustion system.

articles.title: Brent Could Hit $100 Soon
articles.description: Art Hogan, Chief Market Strategist at B. Riley Wealth, projected that the Brent crude oil price could hit $100 in the next week.

articles.title: MOL Completes Unification of Ship Management Units
articles.description: The Japanese maritime leader consummated the combination of six ship management subsidiaries to streamline safety culture.

articles.title: Subsea7 secures contract from LLOG Exploration in US Gulf
articles.description: Subsea7 has secured a contract from LLOG Exploration for offshore work related to the Who Dat East development in the US Gulf of Mexico.

articles.title: Prima Energy to buy 28% stake in Jadestone Energy
articles.description: Prima Energy has signed an agreement to acquire approximately 28.3% of Jadestone Energy’s issued share capital from funds managed by Tyrus Capital.

articles.title: KNOC, Kogas to Merge
articles.description: South Korea will merge a string of state-run energy and transport companies as part of a broader overhaul of public institutions that is aimed at cutting costs and strengthening the country's competitiveness at a time of rising power demand.

articles.title: Chevron to invest more than $7bn in Venezuela oil ventures
articles.description: Chevron has agreed updated terms with Venezuela for its JVs, paving the way for investments of more than $7bn over the next five years.

articles.title: Iraq Hikes Oil Exports via Hormuz in Boon for Asian Refiners
articles.description: OPEC’s second-largest producer, Iraq, more than doubled its crude oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz in August as it offered month-watering discounts for loadings at Basrah in the Persian Gulf and Iran allowed Iraqi oil cargoes to transit the chokepoint. Iraqi oil exports jumped to some 2.34 million barrels per day (bpd) in August from 1.35 million bpd in July, two Iraqi energy officials told Reuters, in data consistent with estimates of vessel-tracking firms Vortexa and Kpler, who see Iraq’s oil shipments at between 2.2 million bpd…

articles.title: Global Refining Crunch Could Keep Fuel Prices High Into 2027
articles.description: Damaged refineries in the Middle East and Russia and insufficient capacity elsewhere to offset the supply disruptions will likely keep global fuel prices elevated into the next year, analysts say. The Middle East conflict and the Iranian and Houthi strikes on Persian Gulf facilities have slashed supply and deliveries from the region, while intensified Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries have prompted a ban on diesel exports out of Russia. As a result, the global fuel markets are tightening, also because capacity elsewhere, including in the…

articles.title: Europe’s Low Gas Stocks Set Stage for Winter LNG Battle
articles.description: Europe’s lowest levels of natural gas in storage in nearly two decades risk intensifying the race for LNG supply in the coming months as both Europe and Asia are competing for a shrinking pool of supply, with the Middle East’s LNG still blocked at the Strait of Hormuz. “The potential for a global ‘fight for fuel’ is there, particularly in a colder winter,” Go Katayama, principal insight analyst for LNG at intelligence firm Kpler, told Bloomberg. Europe is heading into the winter with one of the lowest…

articles.title: Chinese Refiners Pay Record Premiums for Russian ESPO Crude
articles.description: Chinese refiners are paying a hefty premium for Russia’s ESPO crude to replace Iranian crude that independent refiners were importing before the U.S. installed its naval blockade on the country. East Siberia-Pacific Ocean crude, or ESPO, for delivery in November is trading at a premium of over $7 per barrel, with offers reaching as high as $10 per barrel over Brent crude, Bloomberg reported today, citing traders. The blend is loaded from Russia’s Far East coast and can reach the buyers in China in less than a week, the publication noted.…

articles.title: Asian LNG Prices Surge to Highest Since 2022 as Iran War Escalates
articles.description: Spot LNG prices for Asian buyers went up to almost $26 per million British thermal units yesterday for a 5% weekly gain following the resumption of strikes between the United States and Iran. Spot LNG for Asia traded at $25.908 per mmBtu late on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported, citing unnamed traders, after President Donald Trump said “We took out all of the new equipment that they tried to build along the ‌Strait of Hormuz - some defensive, some offensive ... It was a very heavy attack last night, and we're prepared to do another one…

articles.title: Asian Oil Buying Spree Sends Dubai Crude Toward $100
articles.description: Stronger appetite for Middle Eastern crude grades from China and India has added upward pressure on prices for these grades, pushing the Dubai futures close to $100 per barrel, Bloomberg reported today, citing unnamed traders. Demand for Middle Eastern oil is especially strong from refining majors such as Indian Oil Corp. and PetroChina, as well as refiners in South Korea and Japan, the report said. This is despite the latest escalation between the United States and Iran, with Saudi Arabia’s oil exports dropping to the lowest since 2017,…

articles.title: Oil Holds Above $90 as Fighting Flares
articles.description: Oil held near a five-week high as renewed US-Iran fighting raised fresh concerns over Strait of Hormuz exports.

articles.title: Trump Pressures USA Oil Refiners to Ease Pump Prices
articles.description: President Donald Trump pressed U.S. oil refiners to boost domestic production of gasoline and diesel during a closed-door meeting Tuesday.

articles.title: Why Uranium Stocks Are Falling as U.S. Production Triples
articles.description: U.S. uranium production is climbing from a base so depleted that a threefold increase still leaves America dependent on imports for most of its reactor fuel. Output rose to 2.1 million pounds in 2025, its highest level since 2017, before reaching 2.13 million pounds in the first half of 2026, according to the EIA. Second-quarter production increased 4.7% to 1.09 million pounds. U.S. nuclear-plant operators purchased 46.9 million pounds of uranium in 2025, more than 22 times the amount produced domestically. Uranium of U.S. origin accounted for…

articles.title: U.S. SPR Depletion Threatens Further Oil Price Volatility
articles.description: Crude oil prices are on their way up again, driven by the latest flare-up of hostilities in the Persian Gulf—but they are also up because U.S. crude inventories are down again, and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve is moving closer to critical levels. The importance of oil inventories came to the fore soon after the United States and Israel launched their war against Iran at the end of February. It was thanks to these inventories that the world avoided a sharp and painful spike in oil prices. The OECD agreed a controlled release of 400 million…

articles.title: White Hydrogen Drilling Push Gains Momentum Across Three Continents
articles.description: Scientists and start-ups believe naturally occurring hydrogen could be the next major geological breakthrough, unleashing huge amounts of hydrogen to power the clean energy transition. Researchers in the United States, Canada, and Australia are mapping and discovering potential sources of so-called geologic hydrogen, or white hydrogen, which would be mined instead of produced from electrolysis using renewable energy, the way the so-called green hydrogen is currently obtained. articles.title: Superhot Geothermal Just Got A $180 Million Vote Of Confidence
articles.description: As the artificial intelligence boom drives major energy demand growth and catalyzes an all-of-the-above approach to energy development, enhanced geothermal energy is catching a windfall of investment dollars and renewed policy interest. A new wave of next-gen geothermal energy projects and startups may have the backing it takes to bring the cutting-edge, round-the-clock clean energy technology out of the lab and into commercial markets across the United States. Geothermal energy is not a new technology, but its applications are severely limited…

articles.title: SOCAR to Invest in Haynesville with Nearly $1.7B Comstock Partnership
articles.description: The State Oil Company of the Republic of Azerbaijan signed a preliminary deal to acquire a stake in Haynesville gas assets operated by Comstock for $1.65 billion.

articles.title: Texas Oil Regulator Names New Oil, Gas Director
articles.description: David Lindley has been named as the new director of the RRC's Oil and Gas Division.

articles.title: Methanex to Halt NZ Production Indefinitely over Gas Supply Uncertainty
articles.description: The Canadian methanol producer expects to stop production in New Zealand next year and has entered into an agreement selling its gas supply entitlements.
